dev.reply:
Yes
As backend developer, endless regex whack-a-mole makes clean TDD cycles impossible. Replacing the fragile regex with a linear scanner gives us explicit parsing rules and predictable linear execution that we can cleanly unit-test. Defining BLOCKING around real generator corpus shapes and tool output—while demoting contrived compositions to MINOR—removes ambiguity, stops moving goalposts, and lets us comply without gaming reviews. Turning every prior finding into red test rows before green fits our exact development workflow.
CITE: decides each path's extent with explicit rules, so time is linear by construction
